applicability: Fleet agents emitting canonical Learning blocks in field sessions; observed on sde-agents 1.6.0.

evidence.environment: sde-agents 1.6.0, superpowers SDD coordinator session, 26 dispatches
evidence.source_reference: Issue #73 (2026-08-03): 26-dispatch SDD run, five canonical Learning packets emitted and all five discarded

expected_behavior: The handoff is visible where callers actually read: the emitting side points at each packet from its verdict line, and the loop ends with an explicit manifest of packet identifiers, destinations, and dispositions, so a caller that stops mid-contract has visibly stopped.
observation: Learning packets returned to a caller that is a conversation rather than a process have no receiving-side control: a persisted packet and a dropped one produce identical-looking output, so drops stay invisible until someone audits the destination file. Emission was reliable in both observed runs; the loss was entirely on the receiving side.
reason: Triage 2026-08-10: two independent occurrences share the behavior, boundary, and expected result, so this is recurrence rather than an anecdote. Add rather than merge: the loop states that read-only roles return the packet to the caller and stops there, which is correct for foreign repositories but leaves no control when the caller is a conversation; no existing rule covers the receiving side. Not the third self-referential record lc_502daaf warns about, whose theme is this repository's own round-closeout intake; this one is shipped-agent behavior in field sessions. Imported as ACK-001 at decision-needed because the three candidate mechanisms differ in size and only the owner can pick.
